accuracyFlags: 'Designated rest areas along highways permit sleeping for fatigue management, usually up to 24 hours ... the most reliably legal option nationwide' and chip 'Rest areas allow up to 24 hours': Queensland rest areas are signed up to 20 hours (councils can set up to 72), and NSW/VIC/WA limits are set by sign. Some rest areas ban overnight stays (the page's own section 02 says so). Do not state 24 hours as general.
'Council local laws ... many prohibit it in all public places' with no council or state source; page has no 'Check before you go' official-source block (the only rules page of these 12 without one).
FAQ 'sleeping in a vehicle is not itself an offence': true generally but Gold Coast and other council by-laws define sleeping in a vehicle as camping; say so and cite.
Chip 'No engine running for heat' and CO advice are correct; section 08 largely repeats section 07 (duplicate paragraph on shades/mattress).
